entries.title: Wisconsin Democrats Ask Elections Commission to Allow Voters to Recast Absentee Ballots
entries.summary: The bipartisan panel blocked the ability to revote earlier this month after Democrat Missy Hughes exited the governor’s race.
entries.content:
Wisconsin’s gubernatorial candidates keep shuffling before next month’s primary. Now, the state Democratic party is requesting Wisconsin’s elections panel allow voters who already cast an absentee ballot to vote again.

After thousands of Wisconsinites had already submitted their absentee ballots ahead of the Aug. 11 primary, Democrats’ candidate slate shifted twice within days. Front-runner Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez ended her campaign last Friday. A day later, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley rejoined the race a week after he suspended his campaign, reentering with current Wisconsin Gov. Tony Evers’ endorsement.

Earlier this month, the bipartisan Wisconsin Elections Commission blocked the ability to revote if a candidate drops out after a different Democrat, Missy Hughes, exited the governor’s race in June. Because of that ruling, Rodriguez voters and people who would have backed Crowley may have lost their chance to vote for a candidate who will actually be in the running through August, the state Democratic party argues.

Over 80,000 ballots have already been submitted, but the party argues many of these votes are going to waste due to candidates dropping or reentering the race.

The commission voted 4-2 on July 9 to issue the guidance limiting voters’ ability to “spoil” their ballots and excluded circumstances like someone deciding to vote for another candidate.

Wisconsin Democratic Party Chair Devin Remiker said “some voters will not be able to truly participate in our Democratic primary process” if the guidance is not reversed to allow new absentee ballots.

“Allowing voters to spoil and recast their ballots was standard practice in Wisconsin prior to attempts by Republicans to file frivolous lawsuits to muddy the waters,” Remiker said in a statement.

The state Democratic Party argues the new guidance should be rescinded because it reverses the commission’s own rule that was in place in 2022. It is also inconsistent with a 2006 U.S. Supreme Court ruling that stated voting rules should not be changed close to an election, they said.

In the past, Wisconsin voters were able to cancel submitted ballots and then request a new one up to three times, for any reason. But in October 2022, a county circuit judge ruled that this “ballot spoiling” practice was illegal. The 2nd District Court of Appeals reversed the 2022 ruling in February, finding that the lawsuit was not properly served.
entries.author: Torrie Herrington

entries.title: Mamdani Says He Can’t Arrest Netanyahu if He Comes to New York
entries.summary: The New York City mayor posted a two-minute video explaining that he does not have the authority to arrest the Israeli Prime Minister if he comes to New York City.
entries.content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he would not arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu if he comes to New York City, a pledge he made while campaigning for mayor last year.

Netanyahu is expected to visit New York City in September for the annual United Nations General Assembly. Mamdani told The New York Times last week that he was “in active conversation” with the city’s law department over the matter, but said on Tuesday that he does not have the legal authority to enforce the International Criminal Court’s arrest warrant out for Netanyahu. President Donald Trump responded to the mayor’s earlier comments in a Monday Truth Social post, saying the prime minister would not be arrested “in any way, shape or form” in the U.S.

During his mayoral campaign, Mamdani pledged to order the New York Police Department to arrest Netanyahu if he were to come to New York City. He reaffirmed his desire to do so on Tuesday in a two-minute video, calling the prime minister the “architect of a horrific genocide of the Palestinian people.”

“My administration has reviewed every avenue available under applicable law to determine whether New York City could execute the International Criminal Court’s arrest warrant if Benjamin Netanyahu came here,” Mamdani said. “It is clear we do not have the independent legal authority to enforce this warrant.”

He instead turned the onus to arrest Netanyahu onto the federal government, which is unlikely to do so: “I call on them to join the ICC and execute this warrant.”

The International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant in November 2024, accusing them of crimes against humanity including murder, starvation, persecution, and attacks on Gazans.
entries.author: Manuela Silva
